summary: New-entry assessment: rbʕ is absent from glossary lookup. The only securely supported lexical record is mrabʕe “viereckig, quadratisch”, plural adjective of pumpkin-piece shape at JTM 2.12/2. A Turoyo verbal root entry is not established.

Candidate morphological association: II-like m-prefixed shape, possibly borrowed; stem remains unconfirmed. Finite Preterit/Infectum base forms are unrecorded and are not reconstructed. No productive Detransitive or Part. Pass. box is asserted.

The Turoyo coordinates mrabʕe with raqiqe “thin”, following “how do you call them?” and an interviewer’s bracketed suggestion. This is property attribution rather than an event of making square. The cutting event belongs to mqaṭʕiwola, not to mrabʕe.

The input contains two analyzed occurrence records, which each receive a decision. The full verse contains three repetitions, including the bracketed interviewer token; the input’s 1/3 and 2/3 labels do not provide a third analyzable record. No extra decision is fabricated.
Possible Arabic contact and dictionary forms reported by the reader remain research leads, not independently verified etymological evidence in this run. No etymology or base pair is invented.
The four deliverables record the complete new-entry decision: withhold a published verb entry and retain the adjective as an editorial candidate. No sentence is quoted as a verbal example.
Is there an independently attested Turoyo finite rbʕ paradigm with a Preterit/Infectum pair, or is mrabʕe solely a borrowed adjective?
If the adjective is synchronically related to a productive verb, confirm its stem and whether Part. Pass. or Detransitive is appropriate; neither label follows solely from its shape.
Account for the third mrabʕe repetition in any later token audit; this synthesis has decided all two supplied occurrence records.
